sentence: This project studies how reward reactivity, aversive reactivity and executive control combine differently in each individual to drive relapse in dependent alcohol users.
This project uses zebrafish to find lipid metabolites that blood flow forces regulate and that control production of hematopoietic stem cells.
This project studies how adolescent binge drinking causes sex differences in somatostatin neurons and behavior in mice.
This project studies how muscle fibrosis and other biomechanical properties impair muscle function in achalasia.
This project measures congruence of cancer models such as cell lines using molecular profiles from omics and single-cell technologies.
This project studies how molecular movements within a potassium channel regulate cardiac rhythm and how antibody-based tools can restore normal electrical function.
This project tests how subsets of neurons control white adipose tissue lipolysis and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis through sympathetic circuits and affect obesity in mice.
This project explores a T cell therapy for small cell lung cancer that is likely to have fewer side effects than current interventions.
This project studies how maternal and fetal genetic contributions lead to gestational diabetes using high-throughput genomic methods.
This project studies how mutations in a loop of the coronavirus spike affect infection, pathogenesis and transmission.
This project builds tools and databases to extract, analyze, store and share multi-omics, imaging and dosimetry data in radiation oncology.
This project studies how Alzheimer disease risk genes affect brain vascular pathology, using gene editing and screening and then human stem cell and mouse models.
This project studies how autophagy impairment causes selective loss of higher force motor units and respiratory dysfunction in old age.
This project develops genome-editing approaches to understand what ubiquitination events, a type of protein modification, do during flavivirus infection.
This project studies neoantigens and tumor microenvironmental immune cells in small cell lung cancer and how they differ between metastases.
This project tests whether breath biomarkers can distinguish between human metabolic phenotypes and predict insulin sensitivity more accurately than blood-based markers.
This project studies how a protein in mitochondria regulates the function of sebaceous glands, using mouse and human skin research tools.
This project tests whether mutations in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum cause artemisinin resistance and what determines resistance to partner drugs.
This project builds mouse models in which single tyrosines are replaced by phenylalanine in receptor tyrosine kinases to disable one signal transduction axis.
This project tests a platform that isolates tumor-reactive T-cells directly from patient-derived tumor samples in non-small cell lung cancer, without requiring prior antigen knowledge.
